summary: # Marvelous Designer Tips Sharing: Clothing Details Edition Update P18 ## Handling Clothing and Model Overlap Issues P03 ### Folding Sleeves First, draw three inner lines to be folded, then select these inner lines that are slightly wider and cut them. After cutting, you can select these panels separately. We will use the function of shrink and fold the panels more simply and steadily. The reason why we choose to cut and not cut and sew is to prevent the sewing line between the panel and the panel from being affected by the fire. ### Creating the Panel First, make the panel on the top. This panel is the panel on the outside of the fold. After the fire, create the sewing line. Then, use the folding arrangement tool to fold the sleeve panel. After that, print the clothing panel. The printed panel will be harder due to its properties, making it easier to use the folding arrangement tool. ### Using the Folding Arrangement Tool The folding arrangement tool is used to reduce the angle of the sleeve and prevent the fold. The top clothing panel is frozen. Use 120% of the bending force for the first panel. When the force exceeds 100%, the width of the panel will be wider, and the effect will be slightly increased due to hardening. ### Activating and Sewing Panels After freezing the panel, activate the second panel and sew it to the first layer. Repeat this process multiple times to ensure stability and consistency: 1. After freezing the panel, activate the second panel and sew it to the first layer. 2. Repeat this step for additional layers if necessary. Do the same on the other side to increase the shrinkage and hardening. Since the inner layer is sewn directly to the inner layer, it does not need to be frozen. ### Finalizing and Simulating the Design Then, activate the inner layer and sew it to the second layer. Next, add it to the outside and include it in the inside. After finishing, start to simulate. Once the simulation is stable, remove all panels and change the shrinkage rate to 100%, then simulate again. After the simulation stabilizes, remove the hardening and simulate once more. Hide the outer panel to check for folds, and then repeat the process for the inner panel: - After the simulation is stable, please hide the outer panel to check if there is a fold in it or not. - After the simulation is stable, please hide the inner panel to check if there is a fold in it or not. ### Merging Panels and Adjusting Folds After the simulation is stable, reduce the size of the panels and then merge them. Due to the characteristics of the triangular mesh, it may cause folds to form. At this time, select the right button to pop up the reset grid in the menu, and you can rearrange the grid distribution to make the fold position smoother. After folding one side of the sleeve, you can delete the other side of the sleeve and then directly press Ctrl + D to align it to the other side. Adjust the position of the fold in the 3D window and simulate for stability.
